current_answer: Choose cache policy in this order: identify whether the response is private or safely shared; set an explicit freshness lifetime; add ETag or Last-Modified for cheap validation; and permit stale reuse only when the bounded failure/latency trade-off is intended. Use private, no-cache for a personalized response that may remain in a browser, no-store when compliant HTTP caches must not intentionally retain it, and long-lived public caching only for safe or versioned content. Diagnose an old response by separating fresh reuse, stale revalidation, stale serving, browser history/service-worker behavior, and intermediary configuration; inspect request conditionals, Cache-Control, Age, Cache-Status, validators, and the test layer. For a request carrying Authorization, keep a user-specific response private to the browser (or use no-store); a shared cache may reuse an authenticated response only when the response explicitly permits it and the representation and cache key are deliberately safe.

catalogue_card.question: How can web developers choose correct HTTP cache headers and diagnose stale content without accidentally caching private responses?
catalogue_card.text: Separate storage audience, freshness, and validation. Start with private versus shared safety, then use validators and layer-specific evidence.

summary: Fresh reuse may make no network request; stale reuse usually leads to validation.
304 keeps the stored representation while 200 replaces it.
no-cache is not no-store; private is not encryption; s-maxage affects shared caches only.
Authorization changes the shared-cache decision: a private browser cache may retain a user-specific response, while shared reuse needs explicit permission and a safe representation and key.
uncertainty: Standards do not force every cache to store or reuse a response; browser, service-worker, CDN, and vendor behavior varies.
Age and Cache-Status are useful only when exposed by the responding path.
An Authorization header is not a complete privacy control; shared reuse still depends on response directives, cache keys, and deployment configuration.
freshness_note: Bootstrap baseline checked against dated RFC 9111/9110 semantics and developer documentation on 16 Sep 2026; later reports should add rather than rewrite this baseline.
